doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Joe Williams: blues singer, and when they first saw him
summary: They discuss Joe Williams as a blues and ballad singer and how long each had known him.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Was Joe doing — what kind of stuff was he doing at that time?
He wasn’t singing the blues, I’ll tell you that.
Yeah, I was going to ask.

He should have been singing them then. Because that’s his niche. I mean let’s face it. Joe Williams is one of the great blues singers of the time. But he also sings a fine ballad too, you know, and fine jazz songs too, Joe is beautiful.
You know I would like for you to remember when we were with Lunceford’s band and we would go into the Regal Theater and Joe Williams was the stage — I mean wasn’t he working in the theater?
I don’t know. The first time I saw him was with Lionel Hampton that I remember Joe.
Oh, I think this was before Lionel.

He used to tell me that. He used to be backstage when the big bands would come in and he said he was so thrilled when Lunceford came in. And you and I was his same age — he got a year on me, or maybe 6 months.
Six months on you. Yeah my birthday is coming up in a couple of days.
Yeah. He’s got about a year on me. We’re all about the same age.
Oh, that’s right. That’s right, yeah.
